newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Ex-dictator Banzer is assured Bolivian presidency.
newsitem.headline: Ex-dictator Banzer is assured Bolivian presidency.

text.p: Former military dictator Hugo Banzer has assured himself of becoming Bolivia's democratically elected president in August after signing an agreement with two other parties.
Banzer clinched accords late on Wednesday with the Revolutionary Left Movement of former President Jaime Paz Zamora and the populist Solidarity Civic Union led by millionaire Ivo Kuljis.

Banzer, 71, of the right-wing Nationalist Democratic Action Party, came first in presidential elections on Sunday with 22 percent of the vote. Paz Zamora and Kuljis came third and fourth respectively.
Congress selects the winner in early August and Banzer will face Juan Carlos Duran of the ruling, centrist Nationalist Revolutionary Movement (MNR), who came second on Sunday.
The support of the other main parties means Banzer is guaranteed victory.
Banzer led a military regime for seven years after seizing power in a coup in 1971. But despite his human rights record, analysts said, he did well because of his stand on economic issues.
He has endorsed a 12-year-old free-market and privatisation drive that is highly praised by the international financial community.
"I am very happy. I feel that Bolivians across the country should live in peace and dialogue," Banzer said in a brief speech to followers in a La Paz hotel.
He told Reuters his promise to revise privatisation contracts to end monopolies would be carried out by consensus, and would not be bulldozered through by the government.
"The fear that people are attributing to investors is unfounded. What we want to do is accelerate the liberalisation (of the economy)," he said.
"I must remind investors that it was my party which proposed the change of economic model from state capitalism to liberalisation of the economy in 1985," he added.

The present government of mining magnate President Gonzalo Sanchez de Lozada has carried out an ambitious privatisation programme, selling off state oil, telecommunications, electricity firms, and the state railways and airline.
